author: Linnaeus, 1758

art.subject: Red-backed Shrike (Lanius collurio), adult male in spring: crown, nape and rump blue-grey; a black mask from the base of the bill through the eye to the ear-coverts; mantle, scapulars and wing coverts plain chestnut-rufous, without bars; flight feathers dark brown; throat white; breast and flanks washed pale pink; belly white; tail black with white bases to the outer feathers. Bill black and hooked; dark eye; legs black.
art.pose: perched upright on top of a thorny bush, side view
art.scene: Thorny scrub on a Korean offshore island in May, during spring migration, bright light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Small, compact shrike, a little smaller than Bull-headed Shrike, with a fairly big head and a longish tail. Bill short, stout and hooked at the tip. Legs short, dark. Perches upright on bush tops, swinging and fanning the tail. Females are brown above with a brown mask and fine dark crescents on whitish underparts.
avoid: Do not paint black bars on the chestnut back, a thick bill or plain white underparts; those mark Tiger Shrike (Lanius tigrinus).
Do not paint a rufous-brown crown or a rufous tail (Brown Shrike, Lanius cristatus).
Do not paint a rufous crown with a white wing patch (Bull-headed Shrike, Lanius bucephalus).
Do not paint the male's tail brown; it is black with white at the base of the sides.
